findings.title: Prayer possessed, attention turned away
findings.claim: The predicate can portray a settled direction of heart away from the prayer that remains theirs, so the ayah holds continued religious form together with alienated attention.
findings.mechanism: The active participle carries the heedlessness state, while the focus preposition governs the possessed prayer noun with an away-from force. Their prayer remains the named domain even as the predicate directs attention away from it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the construction carries more than a momentary lapse: the prayer stays present as their own while the orientation that should animate it has moved elsewhere.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading, 'they are heedless of their prayer,' remains intact. The durable stance and continued external performance are attributed inferences from the legacy reader walks, not a claim about every instance of forgetfulness.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier, prayer relation, and away-from grammar are supplied, while the directional and durable synthesis comes from unbound reader evidence.

branch_activations.carrier: The active participle form carries a state of heart heedlessness or inattentive drift.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus preposition governs the named prayer noun and contributes an away-from direction; the prayer noun supplies the domain of that state.
branch_activations.activation: Heedlessness therefore contacts a directed relation to their prayer rather than remaining an unlocated lapse.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The group can retain the prayer as its named practice while its attention is turned away from what that practice requires.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet does not establish that every occurrence is durably alienated or that external performance necessarily continues in every case.

branch_activations.activation: The ordinary prayer reference contacts the heedlessness state, allowing the named rite and the departed orientation to remain visible together.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The warning concerns a prayer that is still theirs in form while the heart has moved away from what the prayer gathers and requires.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not replace the prayer sense with a general wish, a prayer-place, or any other available focus-root branch.

findings.title: Ritual movement, ethical stillness
findings.claim: The stillness resonance lets the ayah portray prayer whose bodily form remains while its movement toward vulnerable people has stopped.
findings.mechanism: The focus predicate carries stillness, and the named regulated prayer supplies a practice visibly capable of bodily movement. The surrounding failure to urge, feed, and give aid supplies the independent social field in which that stillness becomes arrested consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold together the performed motions of prayer and the absence of movement toward need, making 'heedlessness' perceptible as ethical inertness rather than mere physical immobility.
findings.containment: The ordinary prayer-and-heedlessness reading remains the floor. The packet does not state that prayer mechanically causes aid; the connection between ritual orientation and social movement is an attributed contextual inference. The separately named cessation-of-motion branch is excluded as an unlanded candidate facet.

epistemic.reason: The focus stillness and prayer carriers are supplied, but the ethical consequence is inferred from legacy reader support and named pericope context.

branch_activations.carrier: The active participle can carry the image of stillness or an unmoved state.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The regulated prayer is placed beside the pericope's failure to urge feeding and its later withholding of aid.
branch_activations.activation: Stillness contacts those social actions as the absence of movement from ritual performance toward the vulnerable.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The ayah can describe prayer that is visibly performed yet ethically unmoved in the direction its surrounding scene makes salient.
branch_activations.boundary: This is not a claim that the prayer has no bodily motion, nor that the contextual relation is a grammatically forced causal chain.

findings.title: Leniency spent inward, denied to need
findings.claim: The overlooking-faults resonance exposes a crooked distribution of leniency: the failure attached to their own prayer is passed over while the orphan's vulnerability meets force.
findings.mechanism: The focus predicate carries easy dealing through overlooking a fault; the possessive prayer relation turns the object inward, while the supplied 107:2 context provides the outward encounter with the orphan. Their contact creates an asymmetry between self-directed ritual tolerance and treatment of dependence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the moral shape of heedlessness as a selective allocation of forbearance, not only as an attentional lapse.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim about being heedless of prayer remains present. The packet does not explicitly state self-exemption, and the citation `د ع ع/B001` is unresolved; the asymmetry is therefore an attributed inference rather than a normalized lexical equation.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and possessive relation are exact, while the social contrast and its inward/outward interpretation come from unbound reader support.

findings.title: The small duty hidden from public sight
findings.claim: The tiny-star resonance turns heedlessness into a failure of perception: public attention catches what is staged while quiet obligations fade from view.
findings.mechanism: The focus predicate carries the image of a tiny, easily missed star. The supplied 107:1 and 107:6 seeing/showing context independently makes visibility the trigger, so the smallness image contacts an attention system that notices the audience and misses unshowy claims.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive orphan, miskin, and ma'un as quiet claims that the public-facing gaze fails to register, while the plain prayer warning remains recoverable.
findings.containment: This is an attributed image-pressure, not a claim that the focus word literally names a star in this sentence. The reader-walk's unresolved auxiliary seeing citation is not normalized, and the small-duty field is not presented as the only meaning of heedlessness.

epistemic.reason: The hidden-star carrier is exact at the focus, while its perceptual and social activation is supplied by unbound reader evidence tied to named pericope ayats.

findings.title: A frontage that filters out the unshowy
findings.claim: The porch-or-rack image makes the focus predicate an attention filter: prayer can be placed on a visible frontage while small household duties remain outside what attention registers.
findings.mechanism: The focus predicate carries the porch or rack as a place where things are set out. The public-display cue of 107:6 and the withheld ma'un of 107:7 independently activate that material image, so visible devotional presentation contacts the exclusion of small practical aid.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see heedlessness as an arrangement of attention that stages what can be seen and screens out what is modest, useful, and close at hand.
findings.containment: The ordinary prayer warning remains intact. The nominated showing-off branch `root_000531/B005` is not activated because no typed context carrier is supplied; public visibility remains an attributed contextual trigger. The frontage is an image-pressure, not a literal architectural claim or a surah-wide system.
